flashcards.q: Is Azure Synapse Analytics deprecated? What's Microsoft's current guidance?
flashcards.a: Not deprecated -- it's in maintenance mode: security/reliability patches continue but no major new capability lands there. All new investment (Copilot, Direct Lake, OneLake, Data Agents, Spark 4.0) goes to Fabric. Guidance: new analytics work starts in Fabric; existing Synapse workloads keep running with a phased migration expected over months to years.

flashcards.q: What is OneLake and why is it Fabric's real architectural differentiator over Synapse?
flashcards.a: One logical, tenant-wide data lake (Delta Parquet format) that every Fabric workload -- Lakehouse, Warehouse, Power BI Direct Lake, Real-Time Intelligence -- reads/writes directly, eliminating cross-engine data duplication. Synapse's separate pools (Dedicated SQL, Serverless SQL, Spark) each typically require real data movement between them.

An F-SKU (F2..F2048, doubling ladder) provisions a fixed Capacity Unit (CU) pool. Every workload in that capacity -- pipelines, Spark jobs, warehouse queries, Power BI refreshes -- draws from the SAME shared CU pool rather than being billed independently.

flashcards.q: How does Fabric throttling actually work, and what production symptom pattern does it cause?
flashcards.a: A smoothing algorithm, not a hard cutoff: sustained usage above capacity delays background operations (pipelines) first, then throttles interactive operations (live reports) only if overage persists. Symptom: slow reports and late pipeline completions appearing around the same time are usually the SAME root cause (capacity pressure), not separate incidents.

flashcards.q: What are the documented Fabric capacity upgrade signals?
flashcards.a: Average CU utilization sustained above 75% for 2+ weeks, more than one throttling event per week at the same time of day, or peak-hour utilization sustained above 150%.

flashcards.q: Contrast Azure Data Factory and Fabric Data Factory billing.
flashcards.a: ADF is standalone, separately provisioned and billed (per activity run, ~$0.274/vCore-hour data flow compute, IR hours). Fabric Data Factory is the same engine but draws compute from the Fabric capacity's shared CU pool -- no separate provisioning, but it competes for capacity with other Fabric workloads like Power BI refreshes.

flashcards.q: What does Event Hubs' Kafka-compatible endpoint actually provide, and what's its real limitation?
flashcards.a: A protocol-compatibility layer -- existing Kafka producer/consumer code points at it by changing only bootstrap server/SASL config, no app rewrite needed for standard produce/consume. It is NOT a literal Kafka broker clone: some admin APIs and exactly-once transactional semantics have gaps versus real Kafka, worth verifying before migration.

flashcards.q: State Event Hubs Standard tier's throughput unit (TU) numbers and throttling behavior.
flashcards.a: 1 TU = up to 1MB/s or 1,000 events/s ingress, up to 2MB/s or 4,096 events/s egress. Self-serve cap 20 TUs (40 via support ticket). Standard tier HARD-THROTTLES at the provisioned ceiling -- no graceful degradation.

flashcards.q: Compare Event Hubs Premium (PU) and Dedicated (CU) tiers to Standard.
flashcards.a: Premium (1-16 Processing Units/namespace) and Dedicated (min 8 Capacity Units, single-tenant) are capacity-based, NOT hard-throttled the way Standard's TU model is -- achievable throughput depends on actual workload shape rather than a fixed per-unit ceiling.

flashcards.q: Contrast Synapse Dedicated SQL Pool and Serverless SQL Pool billing.
flashcards.a: Dedicated SQL Pool is cluster-billed per DWU-hour regardless of query volume (~Redshift). Serverless SQL Pool is billed per TB scanned, query-in-place over lake files with no provisioned cluster (~Athena/BigQuery external tables).

flashcards.q: Map Azure's data stack to AWS/GCP equivalents.
flashcards.a: Synapse Dedicated~=Redshift. Serverless SQL Pool~=Athena/BigQuery external tables. ADF/Fabric Data Factory~=Glue/Dataflow. Event Hubs~=Kinesis (plus a Kafka-compatible endpoint Kinesis lacks). Event Hubs Kafka API~=MSK.
